role_and_message.evidence: The complete two-part framework remains Role-Skill Composition followed by Self-Evolving Orchestration and feedback into the next team-construction round.

panel_and_object_coverage.evidence: Role/skill libraries, original task, orchestrator and checks, three depicted specialists, final answer, rollout selection, within-task reflection, cross-task aggregation and both policy modules all remain.

labels_math_and_numbers.evidence: R, S, x, desc, G, r/s/q indices 1/2/n, d1/d2, final y-hat=dn, rollout tau/v indices, B_t, p_x, L_t, K_t, T_t and pi_t to pi_t+1 retain their original meanings.

connections_and_direction.evidence: Libraries and task feed the orchestrator; outputs from specialists 1 and 2 feed specialist n; execution experience flows down to rollout generation then left through reflection, aggregation and revision, with next-round feedback returning upward to the orchestrator.

visual_encodings.evidence: Blue role and orange skill encodings are consistent across libraries and specialists. Purple policy feedback and teal execution-experience connection preserve original group identities.

examples_and_data.evidence: This is a conceptual agent architecture, without empirical plots or photo evidence. Decorative agent portraits changed while the original roles, three illustrative rollout rows and their symbolic indices remain.

unsupported_additions.evidence: No new scientific component is added. New enclosing box for selected tasks and enhanced arrows organize the same mechanism described by the source Figure 2 and Sections 2.2-2.3.

complete_visible_content.evidence: Both complete stages, all specialist labels, rollout row symbols and policy-update labels are visible and unclipped.

remaining_limitations: Fidelity is to the supplied figure and source description, not validation of the method. Schematic symbols and decorative portraits may change while labels and relations are preserved.

Figure 2: Overview of MASCraft. (1) Role–Skill Composition: the orchestrator agent assigns sub-
tasks, selects role–skill pairs, and establishes information dependencies. (2) Self-Evolving Orches-
tration: within-task reflection and cross-task aggregation distill lessons from contrasting rollouts to
update Environment Knowledge and Team Strategy for subsequent team construction.
